project.name: openmw-config
project.summary: Read, compose and write OpenMW's openmw.cfg chains, as a Jess package in Luau.

notes.summary: `locate` takes the fallbacks it would read from the process, so a tool's tests never find the machine's own OpenMW configuration.
added: `locate(given, fallbacks)`: `fallbacks` is `{ environment, own }`, OPENMW_CONFIG's value and OpenMW's own configuration folder, standing in for this process's. A test passes `{}` to have neither; without it they are read from the process, as in 4.1.0.

notes.summary: Finds OpenMW's own configuration again, as the Rust crate did: `locate` takes a named file or folder, else OPENMW_CONFIG, else the openmw.cfg in OpenMW's user folder.
added: `userFolders()`: the folders OpenMW's `?userconfig?` and `?userdata?` tokens name on this platform, worked out as OpenMW does: Documents\My Games\OpenMW on Windows (the Documents known folder, wherever it was moved), Library/Preferences/openmw and Library/Application Support/openmw on macOS, and the XDG folders elsewhere. Pass them to `new` as `tokens`. Empty without the process.environment capability.
`locate(given)`: the openmw.cfg a tool reads, `given` (a file, or a folder holding one under any capitalization), else OPENMW_CONFIG, else OpenMW's own. Nil and why when there is none.
`@openmw-config/user`: the per-platform rules as a function of a platform description, for a caller describing another platform.
known_issues: `userFolders` and `locate`'s fallbacks need jess 0.2.1 or later, whose runtime says which platform it runs on and where Documents is.

notes.summary: openmw-config is a Jess package, written in Luau; the Rust crate continues on the rust branch at 3.0.2.
breaking: The library is the Jess package `org.dreamweave.openmw-config`, module `@openmw-config`, installed with jess rather than Cargo. The Rust crate `openmw-config` stays at 3.0.2 on crates.io and on this repository's `rust` branch, and is no longer developed on main.

changed: l3i 1.1.0 comes from crates.io; the `@dream/openmw-config` module is unchanged.

notes.summary: The Luau bindings are an l3i extension with live views and typed rows, the loader reads config= chains exactly as OpenMW's engine does, and the site is built with the DreamWeave Mod Template.
added: Typed game setting values and setting metadata, `SettingValue` exported so predicates can name what they are given, and the `meta()` and typed accessors every setting type has.
The views declare their element types, so strict scripts read them directly; items are pushed by value.
A Criterion benchmark for the Luau boundary.
changed: List positions are indexed, game settings iterate without cloning, settings are no longer formatted on load, and the lookup indexes hash with FxHash.
fixed: `save_user`, `save_subconfig` and `Display` keep `replace=` lines; list replacements and removals persist through `replace=` lines in the user config, and a parent's entries stay in the parent's file when the user config replaces a list.
The injected `resources/vfs` data directory is no longer written back as a `data=` line on every save; the directories `resources=` and `data-local=` add stay in step with them.
Windows and macOS fall back to the user config; the `io::Error` behind `ConfigError::Io` is reachable through `source()`.
`add_archive_file` returns `CannotAddArchiveFile` on a duplicate; `replace=fallback-archive` is read and written under the option name OpenMW uses.
`set_game_setting` writes its comments as comment lines, and the comments and blank lines that end a config file survive the settings added after them.

The setting indexes are rebuilt when singleton settings change and after data directories are injected; a parent's relative data directory is written resolved when the user config copies it; a parent's `resources=`, `user-data=`, `data-local=` or `encoding=` stays in place when the user sets one.
The live-view generation counter advances without wrapping, so a stale row can never read as current again.
breaking: The `luau` feature makes the crate an l3i extension, `openmw_config::luau::extension()`, providing the module `@dream/openmw-config`, with live views over the loaded configuration and typed rows. `create_lua_module`, the `mlua` types and the `standalone-lua` feature are gone.
Building with the `luau` feature needs l3i's toolchain: clang, lld and cross-language thin LTO. Rust 1.92.

The loader matches OpenMW's engine: `config=` entries load depth first, each `config=` directory is read once, a `config=` directory without an `openmw.cfg` stays in the chain, the user config directory is created on load, `replace=` applies per config over the configs loaded before it, `replace=config` keeps the root and the `config=` entries still to load, `replace=replace` discards the `replace=` lines of earlier configs, `replace=` values match option names exactly, and `resources=`, `user-data=`, `data-local=` and `encoding=` are left alone by `replace=`.
The crate's internal macros are no longer exported.
Built, released and documented with the DreamWeave Mod Template; the site replaces the rustdoc pages.

notes.summary: First stable release: parsing that matches OpenMW's, Lua bindings, and Flatpak paths.
notes.highlights:
openmw-config 1.0 reads a config chain the way OpenMW does: `config=` entries level by level,
`replace=` applied as it is read, and line numbers in every parse error. It adds embedded Lua
bindings with a camelCase API and resolves tokens correctly inside Flatpak.
added: Lua bindings through `mlua`, behind the `lua` feature: `create_lua_module` and a camelCase API.
Flatpak-aware `?userconfig?` and `?userdata?`, and `OPENMW_FLATPAK_ID`.
`default_local_path` and `default_global_path`, for `?local?` and `?global?`, with fallible `try_` variants.
`user_config_ref`, which leaves the configuration in place, and `&str` views of setting values.
`config_chain`, the parser-order record of loaded and skipped configs.
Parse errors carry the line they came from.
changed: `dirs` and `shellexpand` are replaced by the standard library. On Windows, the Documents folder comes from the Known Folder API.
Queries on content files, archives, data directories and game settings are indexed.
fixed: `config=` entries load level by level, siblings before their children, as OpenMW loads them.
`replace=config` discards earlier settings and queued `config=` entries.
`fallback=` values keep their exact spelling through a round trip.
Game settings are deduplicated by key.
Path comparisons normalize separators.
breaking: Methods that built a `Vec` are gone; collect the iterators instead.
